page: Vultr voc-g-96c-256gb-1280s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance equipped with 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores on an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, featuring two threads per core and dedicated CPU resource allocation. It includes 256.0 GB of memory (2.67 GB per vCPU) and comes bundled with 1280 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. There are no discrete GPUs allocated to this instance.

Benchmark results demonstrate significant compute capacity under dense parallel loads. In multi-threaded testing, the instance scored 213,580.47 in stress-ng multi-core CPU throughput, placing it in the top 10% tier. PassMark tests also indicate strong aggregate compute capabilities, posting scores of 81,703.97 for overall CPU performance, 117,674.91 on extended instructions, and 94,137.55 in encryption workloads. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reached 439.79 GB/sec, matching strong performance tiers. In-memory data store performance is reflected by 101.76 million operations per second on Redis SET tests.

Single-core performance reflects the moderate 2.0 GHz base clock. The single-core stress-ng metric reached 2,460.86, and Geekbench single-core registered at 1,382.0, both falling into the average middle tier. Uncached memory throughput on 256MB blocks registered 145.72 GB/sec for reads and 72.97 GB/sec for writes. Single-threaded gzip compression registered in the bottom 25% at 23.32 GB/sec, illustrating the performance divergence between highly parallel and single-threaded operations.

Given its high core count, high-density multithreaded efficiency, and NVMe local drive, this server fits large-scale batch processing, multithreaded software compilation, high-throughput caching tiers, and multi-tenant container orchestration where aggregate CPU throughput outweighs per-core clock speed.
